extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers, and organizers of PVLDB Scalable Data Science (SDS) submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria specific to submitting and reviewing Scalable Data Science (SDS) papers for the PVLDB / VLDB Research Track, emphasizing practical impact, scalability, and fit with the database/data-management audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical importance and potential for practical impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper did not effectively articulate the practical importance of the problem or the potential for practical impact of the work. This criterion is more important for SDS than Regular, since the latter also focuses on speculative or long-term basic research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should clearly state the practical importance and potential impact. Reviewers and AEs should weigh practical impact heavily for SDS. Avoid submissions that fail to explain why the problem or solution matters in real-world settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evaluation and scalability evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The empirical evaluation was too weak. SDS-specific criteria that were often underappreciated by authors included showing meaningful scalability metrics and use of real-world datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide strong empirical evidence: meaningful scalability measurements, experiments on real-world datasets, and evaluation that demonstrates behavior at scale or in deployed scenarios. Weak or purely synthetic evaluations are an anti-pattern for SDS and a common cause of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of novelty beyond algorithmic novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overemphasize novelty of techniques vs. other valuable forms of novelty, such as a new important problem, new key application impact, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize multiple forms of novelty (new problems, application impact, engineering/empirical insights). Even a simplistic method can be acceptable if it yields interesting insights at scale or in deployed scenarios. Reviewers should be open to these non-algorithmic novelties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to the database/data-management audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper was entirely ML algorithmics-oriented, with little relevance for the database / data management audience. Data Science is broad and PVLDB will not be a suitable venue for many kinds of Data Science papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their submission clearly explains relevance to databases/data management when targeting SDS/PVLDB. Submissions that are purely ML algorithmics without DB relevance are likely to be desk-rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcoming deployed and evaluated solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: As the CFP explains, SDS welcomes submissions of two types: deployed and evaluated solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit deployed systems, tools, or solutions that have been evaluated in practice. Emphasize deployment details, evaluations in real settings, and lessons learned from real-world use when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code release and reproducibility encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: SDS encourages authors to open source their research code and data (or at least make them available privately to reviewers) but this is not mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing open-sourced code/data is encouraged and common among accepted papers (statistics cited: out of 26 accepted papers, 16 provided open-sourced code by submission, 2 shared code privately). If possible, share artifacts to aid reproducibility; if not possible, provide private reviewer access when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer practice: read SDS-specific evaluation criteria and keep an open mind
rubrics_metrics.description: To SDS reviewers: Read the SDS-specific evaluation criteria again before reviewing such papers. Keep an open mind on the various forms of novelty a paper can bring to the table and also its potential for practical impact, especially if it is of the evidential type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should re-familiarize themselves with SDS guidance, be receptive to non-traditional forms of novelty, and consider evidential demonstrations of impact (e.g., deployments, user studies, adoption). During discussions, AEs should recall SDS-specific criteria to guide judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling category fit and reassignment across Research Track categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Some submissions were moved across categories of the Research Track as part of a Revision (e.g., SDS to Regular, SDS to EA&B, or Regular to SDS). Some reviewers found these moves hard to judge due to the differing evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to consider moving submissions across Research Track categories if the paper's merits warrant it, and discuss such moves with Editors in Chief. AEs should help clarify category-specific criteria during deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common reasons for rejection (explicit list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four common reasons observed: (1) lack of articulation of practical importance/impact; (2) empirical evaluation too weak (lack of scalability metrics/real-world data); (3) methods too straightforward/simplistic without other forms of novelty; (4) paper is entirely ML algorithmics-oriented with little DB relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult this list to avoid pitfalls: clearly state impact, strengthen empirical and scalability evidence, justify novelty (or show other valuable contributions), and ensure audience relevance. Reviewers should use these as lenses when assessing SDS fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overemphasizing technique novelty at expense of impact or evidential contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDS-specific guidance required not overemphasizing novelty of techniques vs. other valuable forms of novelty; potential for practical impact and evidential demonstrations should be weighed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing or reviewing submissions, consider practical/evidential contributions (deployments, real usage, measurable impact) as legitimate and sometimes primary forms of contribution for SDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE and organizer recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: To SDS AEs: Recall the SDS-specific evaluation criteria to reviewers when needed during discussions. Keep an open mind on moving a submission across the different categories under the Research Track if the paper’s merits warrant that and after discussing with the Editors in Chief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs should actively guide reviewers toward SDS criteria, facilitate category-appropriate judgments, and refine guidance on technical contributions and scalability as needed for future volumes.
